title: Leaves on the floor: the drift that climbed the trunk
question: Which reads as a forest floor? (real colours, no overlay — the gold is leaf litter)
context_md:
You said the last card looked better but the leaves still didn't look like they
were all on the floor. You were right twice, and I was wrong twice.

**1. The picture I sent you was misleading.** It painted "resting on plant
tissue" in magenta — the same colour for a leaf stuck forty rows up a tree and
for a drift lying on the floor banked against a trunk. The caption said so; a
caption doesn't beat a picture. The overlay now paints on *air underneath*
instead, which is the one thing that isn't confounded. On that measure the
previous fix had already worked: 4 of 497 standing cells held off the ground.

**2. There was still a real defect, and no number in the repo could see it.** A
drift that can't spread sideways has nowhere to go but *up*. Wedged between
trunks it climbed out of the forest floor into the low branches as a column —
touching the ground the whole way, so every measure that asks "what is under
this cell" called it floor. That is the gold mass in one of these panes.

These two panes are **the same scene, same seed, same binary, 12,000 frames**,
with one environment variable turning the new sideways rule on and off. Real
material colours, no markers, no dimming — this is what it looks like. Crop
x120..380, y150..210, at 5x.

|  | as stored A | as stored B |
|---|---|---|
| litter grounded but >8 rows up | 119 (23.9%) | **10 (4.9%)** |
| ...with plant tissue right beside it | 81 of those | 9 of those |
| tallest litter column above terrain | 28 rows | **10 rows** |
| litter within 3 rows of the ground | 43.1% | **73.4%** |
| held off the ground (air underneath) | 0.8% | 0.5% |

Every counter in `examples/ascii` is unchanged except the ant-colony scene's,
which moves because litter is ant food and it genuinely relocated — forage
trips 68 -> 67 against a bar of 8.

The one thing I'd like your eye on beyond the choice: **is the winning floor
too thin?** `litter.ron`'s 42-degree friction angle is there so a drift piles
against a trunk rather than running out to a flat sheet. The new rule only
spills a leaf where there is somewhere lower to go, so drifts should still
form — but this is the trade, and it is yours to call, not mine.
